category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.recovery_moves = ['Body demo each turn.', 'Drill "corner of square".', 'Compare quarter and half.'] — concrete but does not branch by diagnostic, and the trap rationale cites no research even though Grade-3 turn/rotation confusion is well documented (Battista on spatial reasoning; Clements & Sarama on turn-as-rotation).
category_feedback.required_fix: Branch the recovery_moves by what the diagnostic told you: (a) if child does a half when the card says quarter, anchor to the right-angle corner of a sticky-note and have the child press a body part to each side as they turn 90 degrees; (b) if child stops mid-turn or over-rotates past 180, drop back to a clock metaphor (12 to 3 = quarter, 12 to 6 = half) and re-do with the body; (c) if child names the turn but cannot execute it, model with the marker first then have child mirror. Cite Battista (2007) or Clements & Sarama on turn-as-rotation in the rationale so a substitute can see this is a real spatial-reasoning trap, not a vocabulary slip.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Action step 2 has pairs CREATE 2 multistep directions and trade, but the lesson never has children COMPARE different valid routes to the same treasure or refine a strategy — the consolidation discussion_prompts are recall questions ('What's a QUARTER TURN?') not strategy talk. The expanded_walkthrough also does not name the misconception in research-grounded terms (e.g., turn-as-rotation vs turn-as-displacement, Battista 2007).
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a strategy-comparison move in consolidation: pose ONE start/treasure pair on the anchor map and have two pairs share their different valid routes ('Tig went 3-right + quarter + 2-forward; Coco went quarter + 2-forward + 3-right — both land on the treasure. Which uses fewer turns? Which is easier to follow?'). Then in expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the underlying spatial-reasoning principle (turn-as-rotation around the body's vertical axis, per Battista 2007 / Clements & Sarama) so the trap reads as a research-grounded misconception, not a label mix-up.
